bugs.title: Running total overflows int, producing negative levels
bugs.description: `total` is declared `int` on line 13, but it accumulates 40 ADC readings of up to 1023, so the sum can reach ~40920, far beyond the 32767 limit of a 16-bit int. The overflow wraps the sum negative, and averageMm() on line 28 then computes a large negative millimetre value, which is why the firmware printed -3856 mm while the injected level was ~4150 mm (off by ~8000 mm). Firmware printed -3856 mm at 1.02 s while the injected input was 4140.4 to 4169.8 mm: off by 7996.4 mm (tolerance ±40). 10 of 10 values were wrong.

bugs.title: Lamp driven from overflowed average, so it never lights correctly
bugs.description: showLamp() on line 33 compares averageMm() against FULL_MM, but averageMm() returns a negative value because of the int overflow in `total` (line 13/28). The comparison is therefore always false and D6 stays LOW even when the injected level is above 4200 mm, e.g. D6 was not HIGH for 1730 ms in the nominal ramp and 2420 ms in the max/min scenario. D6 was in the wrong state for 350 ms across 2 interval(s), first at 1.50 s: D6 was not HIGH for 180 ms while required (grace 1500 ms).

bugs.title: Relay run length collapses because drive() re-evaluates the hold switch every loop
bugs.description: drive() at lines 46-47 recomputes the relay output from `running && !held()` on every loop iteration, so any read of D3 as LOW (bounce, chatter, or a floating input) immediately forces D6 LOW mid-run instead of letting the 2000 ms run complete. The measured evidence shows pulses of 514 ms, 67 ms, 46 ms and 201 ms instead of 2000 ± 150 ms, and missed starts such as "D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 5.20 s". The run timer in startRun() (lines 29-30) is correct, but the output is gated by an unsynchronised input read rather than by the scheduled state. D6 missed 2 of 11 trigger(s): D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 6.21 s. 25 of 25 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 5.00 s lasted 514 ms, expected 2000 ± 150 ms.

bugs.title: No debounce or state latching on D3 causes relay chatter far above the 2-toggle limit
bugs.description: held() at lines 39-42 reads the raw pin with no debounce, and drive() at lines 46-47 writes D6 on every loop pass, so each bounce edge on D3 toggles the relay directly. The measurements show 16 toggles in a 5000 ms window for button bounce, 6 for hold-then-release, and 28 for rapid chatter around the start, all against a limit of 2. Because the relay output is derived combinationally from the input rather than from a latched run state, contact chatter and mid-run release both produce extra transitions. D6 toggled 16 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 5.00 s (limit 2), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

bugs.title: Presses near the 20 ms settle threshold are missed
bugs.description: The debounce in scanStart() only accepts a press once the raw level has been stable for SETTLE_MS (20 ms), and the check at line 46 uses `now - rawChangedAt >= SETTLE_MS` with rawChangedAt updated only when the sampled level changes (lines 41-45). Because the loop samples asynchronously, a press lasting about 18-22 ms can be released before a stable 20 ms window is ever observed, so openZone() at line 51 is never called; the engine measured "D10 missed 3 of 5 trigger(s): D10 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 500 ms" (also at 2.00 s and 4.00 s). The settle window is too close to the bounce/press duration, so legitimate presses are filtered out instead of only bounce being rejected. D10 missed 3 of 5 trigger(s): D10 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 500 ms.

bugs.title: Horn blast blocks loop and delays button detection
bugs.description: The blast() function uses a blocking delay(HORN_MS) at line 19, so during the 60 ms pulse the loop cannot call scanButton(). Combined with the 15 ms settle window at line 32, a press arriving just after a blast (or during the blocking delay) is not detected until the loop resumes, pushing the D12 HIGH edge past the 100 ms deadline. The measured evidence shows D12 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 2.01 s, missing 1 of 2 triggers. D12 missed 1 of 2 trigger(s): D12 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 2.01 s.
